cues.en: Here, we tackle backpropagation,
cues.zh: 这里，我们要讲反向传播，

cues.en: the core algorithm behind how neural networks learn. After a quick recap for where we are, the first thing I'll do is an intuitive walk through for what the algorithm is actually doing without any reference to the formulas.
cues.zh: 也就是神经网络学习的核心算法。先快速回顾一下我们的进度，然后我会先不涉及公式，直观地带你过一遍这个算法到底在做什么。

cues.en: Then for those of you who do want to dive into the math, the next video goes into the calculus underlying all this.
cues.zh: 然后，对于想深入数学的观众，下一个视频会讲解这一切背后的微积分。

cues.en: If you watched the last two videos or if you're just jumping in with the appropriate background, you know what a neural network is and how it feeds forward information.
cues.zh: 如果你看过前两个视频，或者具备相应背景直接跳到这里，那你已经知道神经网络是什么，以及它如何前向传递信息。

cues.en: Here, we're doing the classic example of recognizing handwritten digits whose pixel values get fed into the first layer of the network with 784
cues.zh: 这里，我们做的是识别手写数字的经典例子，像素值会被输入到网络的第一层，这一层有 784

cues.en: neurons. And I've been showing a network with two hidden layers having just 16 neurons each and an output layer of 10 neurons indicating which digit the network is choosing as its answer.
cues.zh: 个神经元。我一直在展示一个网络，它有两个隐藏层，每层只有 16 个神经元，还有一个 10 个神经元的输出层，用来表示网络选择哪个数字作为答案。

cues.en: I'm also expecting you to understand gradient descent as described in the last video and how what we mean by learning is that we wanna find which weights and biases minimize a certain cost function.
cues.zh: 我也希望你们理解上一个视频里讲的梯度下降，以及我们所说的学习是什么意思：就是找到哪些权重和偏置能让某个代价函数最小。

cues.en: As a quick reminder, for the cost of a single training example,
cues.zh: 快速回顾一下，对于单个训练样本的代价，

cues.en: what you do is take the output that the network gives along with the output that you wanted it to give, and you just add up the squares of the differences between each component.
cues.zh: 你要做的是，把网络给出的输出和你期望它给出的输出，按每个分量求差的平方再相加。

cues.en: Doing this for all of your tens of thousands of training examples and averaging the results,
cues.zh: 对所有数万个训练样本都这样做并取平均，

cues.en: this gives you the total cost of the network.
cues.zh: 就得到网络的总代价。

cues.en: And as if that's not enough to think about, as described in the last video, the thing that we're looking for is the negative gradient of this cost function, which tells you how you need to change all of the weights and biases,
cues.zh: 这还没完——正如上个视频所说，我们要找的是这个代价函数的负梯度，它告诉你需要如何调整所有权重和偏置，

cues.en: all of these connections,
cues.zh: 也就是所有这些连接，

cues.en: so as to most efficiently decrease the cost.
cues.zh: 从而最有效地降低代价。

cues.en: Backpropagation,
cues.zh: 反向传播，

cues.en: the topic of this video, is an algorithm for computing that crazy complicated gradient.
cues.zh: 本视频的主题，是一种用于计算那个极其复杂的梯度的算法。

cues.en: And the one idea from the last video that I really want you to hold firmly in your mind right now is that because thinking of the gradient vector as a direction in 13,000 dimensions is, to put it lightly, beyond the scope of our imaginations,
cues.zh: 而上一期视频里有一个观点，我希望你现在牢牢记在心里：因为把梯度向量看作 13,000 维空间中的一个方向，说得委婉些，已经超出了我们的想象范围，

cues.en: there's another way you can think about it.
cues.zh: 你可以换一种方式来理解它。

cues.en: The magnitude of each component here is telling you how sensitive the cost function is to each weight and bias.
cues.zh: 这里每个分量的幅值，都在告诉你代价函数对每个权重和偏置有多敏感。

cues.en: For example, let's say you go through the process I'm about to describe and you compute the negative gradient and the component associated with the weight on this edge here comes out to be 3.2,
cues.zh: 比如，假设你走一遍我接下来要描述的过程，算出负梯度，那么这条边上的权重对应的分量算出来是 3.2，

cues.en: while the component associated with this edge here comes out as 0.1.
cues.zh: 而这条边对应的分量算出来是 0.1。

cues.en: The way you would interpret that is that the cost of the function is 32 times more sensitive to changes in that first weight.
cues.zh: 你可以这样理解：函数的代价对第一个权重的变化要敏感 32 倍。

cues.en: So if you were to wiggle that value just a little bit, it's gonna cause some change to the cost, and that change is 32 times greater than what the same wiggle to that second weight would give.
cues.zh: 所以如果你稍微扰动一下这个值，就会让代价产生一些变化，而这个变化是对第二个权重做同样扰动所产生变化的 32 倍。

cues.en: Personally, when I was first learning about backpropagation,
cues.zh: 就我个人而言，刚开始学反向传播时，

cues.en: I think the most confusing aspect was just the notation and the index chasing of it all. But once you unwrap what each part of this algorithm is really doing, each individual effect that it's having is actually pretty intuitive. It's just that there's a lot of little adjustments getting layered on top of each other.
cues.zh: 我觉得最让人困惑的就是各种记号，还有到处追下标。但一旦弄清楚这个算法每一部分到底在做什么，它产生的每个单独效果其实都挺直观的。只不过是有很多微小的调整一层层叠加在一起。

cues.en: So I'm gonna start things off here with a complete disregard for the notation and just step through those effects that each training example is having on the weights and biases.
cues.zh: 所以这里我先完全不管记号，直接逐步看看每个训练样本对权重和偏置产生了哪些影响。

cues.en: Because the cost function involves averaging a certain cost per example over all the tens of thousands of training examples,
cues.zh: 因为代价函数涉及对全部数万个训练样本中每个样本的某项代价求平均，

cues.en: the way that we adjust the weights and biases for a single gradient descent step also depends on every single example.
cues.zh: 所以我们为单次梯度下降步骤调整权重和偏置的方式，也依赖于每一个样本。

cues.en: Or rather, in principle, should, but for computational efficiency, we're gonna do a little trick later to keep you from needing to hit every single example for every single step. In other case, right now, all we're gonna do is focus our attention on one single example,
cues.zh: 更准确地说，原则上应该如此，但为了计算效率，我们之后会用一个小技巧，让你不必在每一步都遍历每一个样本。换句话说，现在我们要做的只是把注意力集中在一个样本上，

cues.en: this image of a two.
cues.zh: 这张数字 2 的图像。

cues.en: What effect should this one training example have on how the weights and biases get adjusted?
cues.zh: 这个训练样本应该对权重和偏置的调整方式产生什么影响？

cues.en: Let's say we're at a point where the network is not well trained yet, so the activations in the output are gonna look pretty random. Maybe something like 0.5,
cues.zh: 假设现在网络还没训练好，所以输出层的激活值看起来会相当随机。可能是 0.5，

cues.en: on and on.
cues.zh: 等等。

cues.en: Now we can't directly change those activations. We only have influence on the weights and biases,
cues.zh: 现在我们不能直接改变那些激活值。我们只能影响权重和偏置，

cues.en: but it is helpful to keep track of which adjustments we wish should take place to that output layer.
cues.zh: 但记录下我们希望输出层发生哪些调整是有帮助的。

cues.en: And since we want it to classify the image as a two, we want that third value to get nudged up while all of the others get nudged down.
cues.zh: 既然我们希望它把这张图分类为数字2，我们就希望第三个值被往上推，而其他所有值都被往下压。

cues.en: Moreover,
cues.zh: 而且，

cues.en: the sizes of these nudges
cues.zh: 这些调整的幅度

cues.en: should be proportional to how far away each current value is from its target value.
cues.zh: 应该与每个当前值距离其目标值的远近成正比。

cues.en: For example, the increase to that number two neuron's activation
cues.zh: 例如，数字2那个神经元的激活值增加

cues.en: is in a sense more important than the decrease to the number eight neuron, which is already pretty close to where it should be.
cues.zh: 在某种意义上比数字8神经元的减小更重要，因为后者已经相当接近它应该在的位置了。

cues.en: So zooming in further, let's focus just on this one neuron, the one whose activation we wish to increase.
cues.zh: 再放大一点，我们只看这一个神经元，也就是我们希望提高其激活值的那个。

cues.en: Remember,
cues.zh: 记住，

cues.en: that activation is defined as a certain weighted sum of all of the activations in the previous layer plus a bias,
cues.zh: 这个激活值定义为上一层所有激活值的某个加权和，再加上一个偏置，

cues.en: which has all been plugged into something like the sigmoid squishification function or a ReLU.
cues.zh: 然后整体输入到类似 sigmoid 压缩函数或 ReLU 之类的函数里。

cues.en: So there are three different avenues that can team up together to help increase that activation.
cues.zh: 所以有三条不同的途径可以共同作用，帮助提高这个激活值。

cues.en: You can increase the bias,
cues.zh: 你可以增大偏置，

cues.en: you can increase the weights, and you can change the activations from the previous layer.
cues.zh: 你可以增大权重，也可以改变上一层的激活值。

cues.en: Focusing just on how the weights should be adjusted, notice how the weights actually have differing levels of influence.
cues.zh: 先只关注权重该如何调整，注意权重的实际影响程度并不相同。

cues.en: The connections with the brightest neurons from the preceding layer have the biggest effect since those weights are multiplied by larger activation values.
cues.zh: 与上一层中最亮神经元相连的连接影响最大，因为这些权重会乘以更大的激活值。

cues.en: So if you were to increase one of those weights, it actually has a stronger influence on the ultimate cost function than increasing the weights of connections with dimmer neurons,
cues.zh: 所以，如果你增大其中一个权重，它对最终代价函数的影响，会比增大与较暗神经元相连的权重更强，

cues.en: at least as far as this one training example is concerned.
cues.zh: 至少对这个训练样本来说是这样。

cues.en: Remember, when we talk about gradient descent,
cues.zh: 记住，当我们讨论梯度下降时，

cues.en: we don't just care about whether each component should get nudged up or down.
cues.zh: 我们不只关心每个分量该往上调还是往下调。

cues.en: We care about which ones give you the most bang for your buck.
cues.zh: 我们关心的是哪些分量能带来最大的收益。

cues.en: This, by the way, is at least somewhat reminiscent of a theory in neuroscience for how biological networks of neurons learn, Hebbian theory, often summed up in the phrase neurons that fire together wire together.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这至少有点让人联想到神经科学中关于生物神经元网络如何学习的一种理论，即赫布理论，常被概括为一句话：一起放电的神经元会连接在一起。

cues.en: Here, the biggest increases to weights, the biggest strengthening of connections
cues.zh: 在这里，权重增幅最大、连接增强最强的情况

cues.en: happens between neurons which are the most active and the ones which we wish to become more active.
cues.zh: 发生在最活跃的神经元，以及我们希望变得更活跃的神经元之间。

cues.en: In a sense, the neurons that are firing while seeing a two get more strongly linked to those firing when thinking about a two.
cues.zh: 某种意义上，看到数字二时活跃的神经元，会与思考二时活跃的神经元建立更强的连接。

cues.en: To be clear, I really am not in a position to make statements one way or another about whether artificial networks of neurons behave anything like biological brains, and this fires together, wire together idea comes with a couple meaningful asterisks.
cues.zh: 需要说明的是，我其实没有资格断言人工神经元网络的行为是否真的像生物大脑，而且"一起激发、连在一起"这个说法还带有几个值得注意的保留。

cues.en: But taken as a very loose analogy, I do find it interesting to note.
cues.zh: 但作为一个非常粗略的类比，我觉得这点确实挺有意思。

cues.en: Anyway,
cues.zh: 总之，

cues.en: the third way that we can help increase this neuron's activation
cues.zh: 第三种帮助提高这个神经元激活值的方法

cues.en: is by changing all the activations in the previous layer.
cues.zh: 是改变前一层中所有的激活值。

cues.en: Namely, if everything connected to that digit two neuron with a positive weight got brighter,
cues.zh: 也就是说，如果所有以正权重连接到那个数字 2 神经元的东西都变亮，

cues.en: and if everything connected with a negative weight got dimmer,
cues.zh: 而所有以负权重连接的东西都变暗，

cues.en: then that digit two neuron would become more active.
cues.zh: 那个数字 2 神经元就会变得更活跃。

cues.en: And similar to the weight changes, you're gonna get the most bang for your buck by seeking changes that are proportional to the size of the corresponding weights.
cues.zh: 和权重变化类似，寻找与对应权重大小成比例的变化，能让你获得最大收益。

cues.en: Now, of course, we cannot directly influence those activations.
cues.zh: 当然，我们无法直接影响那些激活值。

cues.en: We only have control over the weights and biases.
cues.zh: 我们只能控制权重和偏置。

cues.en: But just as with the last layer, it's helpful to just keep a note of what those desired changes are.
cues.zh: 但和最后一层一样，记下这些期望的变化会很有帮助。

cues.en: But keep in mind, zooming out one step here, this is only what that digit two output neuron wants.
cues.zh: 但请记住，这里退一步看，这仅仅是那个数字 2 输出神经元想要的结果。

cues.en: Remember, we also want all of the other neurons in the last layer to become less active,
cues.zh: 记住，我们也希望最后一层所有其他神经元变得不那么活跃，

cues.en: and each of those other output neurons has its own thoughts about what should happen to that second to last layer.
cues.zh: 而这些其他输出神经元中的每一个，都对倒数第二层该发生什么有自己的想法。

cues.en: So the desire of this digit two neuron is added together with the desires of all the other output neurons
cues.zh: 所以，这个数字 2 神经元的期望，会和所有其他输出神经元的期望加在一起

cues.en: for what should happen to this second to last layer.
cues.zh: 来决定倒数第二层应该发生什么。

cues.en: Again, in proportion to the corresponding weights and in proportion to how much each of those neurons needs to change.
cues.zh: 同样，与对应权重成正比，也与每个神经元需要改变的程度成正比。

cues.en: This right here is where the idea of propagating backwards comes in.
cues.zh: 这里就引出了反向传播的思想。

cues.en: By adding together all these desired effects, you basically get a list of nudges that you want to happen to the second to last layer.
cues.zh: 把所有期望效果加在一起，你基本上就得到了一串想让倒数第二层发生的微调。

cues.en: And once you have those, you can recursively apply the same process to the relevant weights and biases that determine those values, repeating the same process I just walked through and moving backwards through the network.
cues.zh: 一旦得到这些，你就可以把同样的过程递归应用到决定这些值的相关权重和偏置上，重复我刚才讲过的过程，并在网络中反向推进。

cues.en: And zooming out a bit further, remember that this is all just how a single training example
cues.zh: 再拉远一点看，记住这一切都只是一个训练样本

cues.en: wishes to nudge each one of those weights and biases. If we only listen to what that two wanted, the network would ultimately be incentivized just to classify all images as a two.
cues.zh: 希望如何微调每一个权重和偏置。如果我们只听从那个“2”的意愿，网络最终就会被激励把所有图像都分类成 2。

cues.en: So what you do is you go through this same back prop routine for every other training example, recording how each of them would like to change the weights and the biases,
cues.zh: 你要做的就是，对每一个其他训练样本都走一遍同样的反向传播流程，记录每个样本希望如何改变权重和偏置，

cues.en: and you average together those desired changes.
cues.zh: 再把这些期望的变化平均起来。

cues.en: This collection here of the averaged nudges to each weight and bias is loosely speaking, the negative gradient of the cost function referenced in the last video or at least something proportional to it. I say loosely speaking only because I have yet to get quantitatively precise about those nudges. But if you understood every change that I just referenced, why some are proportionally bigger than others, and how they all need to be added together, you understand the mechanics for what backpropagation
cues.zh: 这里收集到的、对每个权重和偏置的平均微调量，粗略地说，就是上一个视频中提到的代价函数的负梯度，或者至少是与其成比例的某个量。我说“粗略地说”，只是因为我还未对这些微调量做定量精确描述。但如果你理解了我刚才提到的每一个变化、为什么有些按比例更大，以及它们如何都需要加在一起，你就理解了反向传播的机制

cues.en: is actually doing.
cues.zh: 实际上正在做什么。

cues.en: By the way, in practice, it takes computers an extremely long time to add up the influence of every single training example, every single gradient descent step.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，实际中，计算机要累加每一个训练样本、每一个梯度下降步骤的影响，会花费极其漫长的时间。

cues.en: So here's what's commonly done instead.
cues.zh: 所以通常的做法是这样。

cues.en: You randomly shuffle your training data and then divide it into a whole bunch of mini batches.
cues.zh: 你把训练数据随机打乱，然后分成一大堆小批量。

cues.en: Let's say each one having a 100 training examples.
cues.zh: 假设每个小批量有 100 个训练样本。

cues.en: Then you compute a step according to the mini batch. It's not gonna be the actual gradient of the cost function, which depends on all of the training data, not this tiny subset.
cues.zh: 然后你根据这个小批量计算一步。它不会是代价函数的真实梯度，因为真实梯度取决于全部训练数据，而不是这个很小的子集。

cues.en: So it's not the most efficient step downhill,
cues.zh: 所以这算不上最高效的下山步伐，

cues.en: but each mini batch does give you a pretty good approximation.
cues.zh: 但每个小批量确实能给你一个相当不错的近似。

cues.en: And more importantly, it gives you a significant computational speed up. If you were to plot the trajectory of your network under the relevant cost surface, it would be a little more like a drunk man stumbling aimlessly down a hill, but taking quick steps rather than a carefully calculating man determining the exact downhill direction of each step before taking a very slow and careful step in that direction.
cues.zh: 更重要的是，它带来了显著的计算加速。如果你在相关代价曲面上画出网络的轨迹，它更像一个醉汉跌跌撞撞、漫无目的地往山下走，只不过步子很快；而不像一个精打细算的人，每走一步前都先确定精确的下山方向，再朝那个方向非常缓慢而小心地迈出一步。

cues.en: This technique is referred to as stochastic gradient descent.
cues.zh: 这种技术被称为随机梯度下降。

cues.en: There's kind of a lot going on here, so let's just sum it up for ourselves, shall we? Backpropagation
cues.zh: 这里涉及的内容有点多，所以我们自己来总结一下，好吗？反向传播

cues.en: is the algorithm for determining how a single training example would like to nudge the weights and biases,
cues.zh: 是用来确定单个训练样本想要如何微调权重和偏置的算法，

cues.en: not just in terms of whether they should go up or down, but in terms of what relative proportions to those changes cause the most rapid decrease to the cost.
cues.zh: 不只是看它们该升还是该降，还要看这些变化按什么相对比例能让代价下降得最快。

cues.en: A true gradient descent step would involve doing this for all your tens and thousands of training examples and averaging the desired changes that you get. But that's computationally slow,
cues.zh: 真正的梯度下降步骤，需要对你成千上万个训练样本都这样做，并对得到的期望改动取平均。但这样在计算上很慢，

cues.en: so instead you randomly subdivide the data into these mini batches and compute each step with respect to a mini batch.
cues.zh: 所以改为把数据随机划分成这些 mini-batch，并基于每个 mini-batch 计算每一步。

cues.en: Repeatedly going through all of the mini batches and making these adjustments,
cues.zh: 反复遍历所有 mini-batch 并进行这些调整，

cues.en: you will converge towards a local minimum of the cost function, which is to say your network is gonna end up doing a really good job on the training examples.
cues.zh: 你就会逐渐收敛到代价函数的局部最小值，也就是说，你的网络最终会在训练样本上表现得非常好。

cues.en: So with all of that said, every line of code that would go into implementing backprop
cues.zh: 所以说，实现反向传播的每一行代码

cues.en: actually corresponds with something that you have now seen, at least in informal terms.
cues.zh: 其实都对应着你已经见过的某个东西，至少是粗略层面上的对应。

cues.en: But sometimes knowing what the math does is only half the battle, and just representing the damn thing is where it gets all muddled and confusing.
cues.zh: 但有时候，知道数学在做什么只是成功的一半，真正把这玩意儿表示出来，才是一团乱麻、让人犯晕的地方。

cues.en: So for those of you who do want to go deeper, the next video goes through the same ideas that were just presented here, but in terms of the underlying calculus, which should hopefully make it a little more familiar as you see the topic in other resources.
cues.zh: 所以，对于想更深入的同学，下一个视频会讲刚刚展示过的同样这些思想，但会从底层的微积分角度来讲，希望这样能让你从其他资料中看到这个话题时觉得更熟悉一些。

cues.en: Before that, one thing worth emphasizing is that for this algorithm to work, and this goes for all sorts of machine learning beyond just neural networks, you need a lot of training data. In our case, one thing that makes handwritten digits such a nice example is that there exists the MNIST database with so many examples that have been labeled by humans. So a common challenge that those of you working in machine learning will be familiar with is just getting the labeled training data that you actually need, whether that's having people label tens of thousands of images or whatever other data type you might be dealing with.
cues.zh: 在此之前，有一点值得强调：要让这个算法奏效，你需要大量训练数据；这不仅适用于神经网络，也适用于神经网络之外的各种机器学习。在我们的例子中，手写数字之所以是个很好的示例，是因为有 MNIST 数据库，里面有大量由人工标注的样本。所以，从事机器学习的人都会熟悉的一个常见挑战，就是获得你真正需要的已标注训练数据——无论是让人标注数万张图像，还是处理你可能遇到的其他任何数据类型。
